The independently evidenced English base gloom is the actual root; gl is only a phonestheme, not the claimed morpheme. The source groups English words by shared gl- letters but does not establish gl as an independently meaningful morphological root. Linguistic research treats /gl/ in many light/vision words as a phonestheme, whose status differs from an ordinary separable morpheme; etymology and senses vary across words. This specific item belongs to the independently attested English lexical base gloom. The proposed corrected edge is a separate review, not an acceptance of gl. Modern gloom is probably from a sullen-looking verb of uncertain origin; its similarity to glow is not proof of their being the same root.
